core.title: Keep telemetry vendor SDK imports out of core layers
core.given: A source file assigned to a core layer role — any layer role other than integration (domain, application, presentation, composition root) — and not inside the adapter location.
core.when: it imports — as a value or only as a type — a package on the profile's telemetry vendor SDK list.
core.then: The file MUST NOT import a telemetry vendor SDK.
prefer: Depend on the port; adapt at the edge: core takes a neutral telemetry port as a parameter and emits through it — no vendor SDK.
Put the vendor SDK in an adapter at the outer ring — the integration layer or the adapter location; the SDK lives there and only there.
avoid: Type-only vendor imports in core layer roles: the coupling is real even when erased.
Relabelling or moving a file just to escape the check instead of splitting port and adapter.
unless: Integration layer or adapter location: exempt by design, the adapter belongs there.
Files with no role assignment (unlayered entrypoints such as the composition root wiring or scripts): outside this rule — they wire adapters, they do not become one.
Inert until adoption, like every rule in this family.
core.why: Core depends only on a neutral telemetry port; once a domain module imports an exporter, every module behind it inherits the vendor and exporter-neutrality is gone.
evidence: The telemetry vendor-import check reports no finding for files in core layer roles outside the integration layer and the adapter location.
Review: no value or type-only vendor SDK import exists in domain, application, presentation or composition-root files outside the adapter location.
Core telemetry emission goes through a neutral telemetry port dependency; the vendor SDK appears only in an integration-layer or adapter-location adapter.
verification: Scope: source files assigned to a layer role; a vendor SDK import is allowed only when the role is integration or the file sits inside the adapter location.
Files with no role assignment (unlayered entrypoints, scripts) are not checked.

The check examines each in-scope file's current imports — pre-existing imports, newly added imports, and files newly moved into a core layer — not only added lines; an import-level observer is required.
Rule is inert until the repository adopts it (family-wide adoption gate).
Strict disposition: the checker fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline (severity 2).
The vendor SDK specifiers and the adapter location are stack data supplied by the profile; the stack's checker owns their exact matching.

values: file contains an import (value or type-only) of a package on the profile's telemetry vendor SDK list

fires: A domain-role file imports a vendor SDK to emit a span directly.
An application-role file imports a vendor SDK only as a type (type-only still counts).
A presentation-role file imports a product-analytics vendor SDK to track an event.
A file that already imports a vendor SDK is moved from the integration layer into a core layer role.
doesNotFire: An integration-layer file imports a vendor SDK to implement the telemetry port adapter.
A file inside the adapter location imports a vendor SDK.
An unlayered composition root or script imports a vendor SDK to wire adapters.
A domain file imports only the neutral telemetry port type.
The repository has not adopted this rule family (rule is inert).

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's layer roles and their local names; the rule's scope is every layer role except integration (the core layers).
How a file is assigned to a layer role, and that a file with no role is out of scope (not checked, not a violation).
profileRequirements.bunValue: the path's layer segment; unlayered files (no layer segment, e.g. composition root, scripts) are not checked

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's local name for the composition-root layer, which is in scope like the other core layers.
The telemetry vendor SDK import specifiers (exporters, agents, product-analytics packages; bare and scoped names) whose import — value or type-only — is forbidden in core layer roles.
profileRequirements.bunValue: @opentelemetry/*, @sentry/*, @datadog/*, dd-trace, newrelic, segment (bare or @segment/*), mixpanel (bare or @mixpanel/*), amplitude (bare or @amplitude/*), @posthog/*, @statsig/*, @braze/*, @heap/*, @rudderstack/*

profileRequirements.meaning: The directory where adapters that wire external SDKs to neutral ports live; files there are exempt from the core-layer import prohibition, like integration-layer files.

proposedKeys.meaning: Import specifiers of telemetry vendor SDKs (exporters, agents, product-analytics packages; bare and scoped names) that core layer roles must not import.
proposedKeys.bunValue: @opentelemetry/*, @sentry/*, @datadog/*, dd-trace, newrelic, segment (bare or @segment/*), mixpanel (bare or @mixpanel/*), amplitude (bare or @amplitude/*), @posthog/*, @statsig/*, @braze/*, @heap/*, @rudderstack/*
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.forbidden_runtime_imports covers runtime, framework and transport specifiers, not telemetry exporter/agent packages; no other key carries a category-specific forbidden-package list.

proposedKeys.meaning: Directory where adapters that wire external SDKs to neutral ports live; files there are exempt from core-layer import prohibitions, like integration-layer files.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The closed role params have no adapter/infrastructure role, so roles.<role>.path cannot express it, and no layout key records the adapter directory.

neutralityNotes: The concrete telemetry vendor package list and the adapter directory are stack data with no existing vocabulary key, so two keys are proposed (idiom.telemetry_vendor_sdks, layout.adapter_dir) and also listed in profileRequirements; without owner approval the Bun values remain the reference instantiation. 'Type-only import' is retained as a cross-stack concept (a compile-time-only dependency still couples); the concrete syntax (import type) stays in bun.json. The activation examples' concrete package names and import statements are instantiation only — the core keeps role-level fires/doesNotFire and bun.json remains the worked example. The project-local port name TelemetryPort is generalized to 'a neutral telemetry port'. Severity, strict disposition, the adoption gate and the import-level observer requirement are per-rule verification facts and stay in the core, not the profile.
